solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shades they take off at the end of strip

definitions.meaning: shades are sunglasses, and the aviator style is a classic pair

definitions.text: they take off at the end of strip
definitions.meaning: pilots launch their planes from the end of an airstrip

explanation.surface: Something that peels off at the close of a striptease act, as if a performer were shedding garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' suggests undressing, but it is a runway; the second reading describes pilots lifting off from an airstrip.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a style of pilot-inspired sunglasses, and the flyers themselves who leave the runway.

clue.text: Navy intercepts the fifth-to-last letter he wrote

indicators.note: to intercept is to cut into the path of something, so the navy letters go inside the spelt-out letter

parts.note: counting back from Z, the fifth-to-last letter of the alphabet is V, spelt out as vee
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A navy vessel stops a letter in transit, the fifth from the end of some correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' tempts as a piece of mail; counting back from Z it is the alphabet's V, and only its spelt-out name leaves room to be intercepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne was a French novelist, so 'he wrote' is a person defined by his writing career.

clue.text: Engineered canoe raced across lake with increasing speed

indicators.note: the reworked letters stretch across, that is around, the lake letter
engineered means contrived or reworked, so the letters of canoe raced are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A boat built for the purpose sped across a lake, going faster and faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineered' rearranges CANOE RACED and 'across' puts that mix around L.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical direction tells players to quicken the tempo gradually, from the Italian for accelerating.

clue.text: Finished parties on ecstasy, too much of it perhaps

parts.note: something finished is over
dos are parties or celebrations
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Partying is done after a night on ecstasy, perhaps having taken too much of the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking an excessive, dangerous quantity of a drug is the medical sense of the word; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of excess.

clue.text: Standard of best beach rubbish close to piers

parts.note: the star of a team is its best performer
the sands are a beach
tripe is nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here the end of piers

explanation.surface: Seaside litter piling up by the piers is the standard of the finest beaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a flag, not a level of quality, which is what the surface wants it to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, and this is the popular name for the United States flag.

clue.text: The male in ultimate command

indicators.note: in says the male pronoun sits inside the word for ultimate

parts.note: the ultimate thing is the best of all
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man holds the highest authority, the ultimate commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is an order or instruction, as in doing something at someone's bidding.

clue.text: Dispute below Polish northbound tunnel

indicators.note: in a down answer the dispute word comes below the other piece
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word for polish is reversed

parts.note: to polish is to rub
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A quarrel underground about a Polish tunnel heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' poses as the nationality; it is the verb to rub, read upwards by 'northbound' to give BUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals such as rabbits dig a hole or tunnel underground to live in, both noun and verb.

clue.text: What's done to convert ships to subs for operation

definitions.text: What's done to convert ships to subs
definitions.meaning: change the middle letters of ships to give subs: the swap of one letter group for another
a surgical procedure in which a worn joint is renewed

explanation.surface: A naval refit question: what work turns surface ships into submarines?
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is wordplay in disguise: take S-HIP-S, put UB in place of HIP, and you have SUBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons commonly renew a worn hip joint with an artificial one, a routine orthopaedic procedure.

clue.text: Labour supports second family getting transplant

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath the others

parts.note: kin are one's family
graft is hard work or labour

explanation.surface: Labour's backing for a second family receiving a transplant, as though a party were funding surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party; it is graft, hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: This is surgery that moves healthy tissue from one site to cover a burn or wound, a kind of transplant.

clue.text: Source of omens vaguely clear

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its opening letter
vaguely means in a loose, unclear way, so the letters of clear are jumbled

explanation.surface: A provider of prophecies whose pronouncements are only vaguely clear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: O from 'Source of omens' plus 'vaguely' rearranging CLEAR to RACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: At Delphi a priestess gave cryptic prophecies, so such a seer is a source of omens with famously ambiguous answers.

clue.text: Indian city character with a writing disorder

parts.note: Agra is the city in India home to the Taj Mahal
phi is a character of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A person from an Indian city who has trouble writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person, but it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medical term for losing the ability to write, usually through brain injury.

clue.text: Scale of fish on front of pinnie

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it
the front of a word is its first letter, here the start of pinnie

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish scale stuck to the front of a cook's apron.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinnie is a pinafore, a British word for an apron.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a fish or to strip off its skin are both ways of removing an outer layer, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Put off record given the years we've been around

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
the number of years we have lived is our age

explanation.surface: Records from our generation could deter a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone or dishearten them from acting is a synonym of putting them off.

clue.text: See 7
Rascal recalled man's address working in jail

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the form of address is reversed

parts.note: sir is the polite way to address a man
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A rascal in a working prison remembers how he spoke to a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to lock someone up behind bars.

clue.text: Brilliant car bishop nicked from funeral

parts.note: a Merc is short for a Mercedes car

indicators.note: nicked means stolen, so the bishop letter is taken away from the funeral word

parts.note: a burial is a funeral
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A splendid car belonging to a bishop is stolen from a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked from' takes B out of BURIAL, leaving URIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a quick, lively, sparkling temperament, like quicksilver, which supports the sense of brilliant.

clue.text: Heartless Trojan means to transport infants

indicators.note: heartless means losing its centre, so the middle letter of the king's name goes

parts.note: Priam was the king of Troy

explanation.surface: A cruel Trojan's way of moving children around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the central I out of PRIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby carriage is a vehicle pushed along to carry babies; 'means' here is a noun, a device.

clue.text: Part of the Woodwork and Brass Co. organised run

indicators.note: organised means sorted into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A firm of woodworkers and brass fitters is set up and run.
explanation.walkthrough: In football 'the woodwork' is the goal frame, posts and bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizontal bar joining the goalposts belongs to what commentators call the woodwork.

clue.text: Architect's painful separation having lost children

indicators.note: having lost means without, so the letters for children are taken away

parts.note: a wrench is an emotionally painful parting

explanation.surface: An architect's heartbreaking split after losing his children.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren was the designer of St Paul's Cathedral and many London churches.

clue.text: Palace staff maybe shot ravens outside of towers

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters of ravens are scrambled
the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The ravens of the Tower of London, shot outside its towers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tower of London famously keeps ravens.
explanation.definitionFit: Household employees are one example of the people working at a royal palace, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Publisher is someone who has gone to court

parts.words: someone who has gone to court
parts.note: a person who sues brings a case to court

explanation.surface: A publisher is someone who has been taken to court.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher puts out or releases books and statements, which is to issue them.

clue.text: A bit unwell without fixes

parts.note: being out of something means being without it
to sort something is to fix it

explanation.surface: Feeling slightly ill because one has no remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone feeling slightly ill or in a bad mood.

clue.text: Panto figure cycling for cheese

indicators.note: cycling sends the last letter round to the front of the word

parts.note: the dame is a stock character of British pantomime, played by a man

explanation.surface: A pantomime character going round on a bike for some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final E of DAME round to the front. Pantomime is a British family Christmas show.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coat.

clue.text: Withdrawn dessert, American upset

indicators.note: in a down answer upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: a fool is a dessert of fruit and cream

explanation.surface: A dessert is taken off the menu and an American is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved, standoffish person keeps to themselves, distant and detached.

clue.text: School mostly nervous delivering event with a bar

parts.note: a high is a high school, often called just the High

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word for nervous goes

parts.note: jumpy means nervous

explanation.surface: A mostly nervous school putting on a sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: In this athletics event competitors leap over a horizontal bar set ever higher.

clue.text: It's cast from lead in hot old flame

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter, the one at the front

parts.note: an ex is a former lover

explanation.surface: Something cast in molten lead, poured from a hot old fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' and 'lead' suggest metal foundry work; a spell is what is cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch casts a curse or spell, so this jinx is something that is cast.

clue.text: French person connects fibre to network

indicators.note: the answer joins up the end of one word, a whole word and the start of another, connecting them

explanation.surface: A man in France links up broadband fibre to the network.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'fibRE TO Network', starting inside fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Brittany in north-west France is a French person of a particular region.

clue.text: Special FX role for contractor

indicators.note: special is read as specially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A special effects job going to a building contractor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contractor' looks like a builder; it is a muscle that contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle that bends a joint does so by contracting, so it is literally something that contracts.

clue.text: Flipped cakes with one extremely fruity layer

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the word for cakes is read backwards

parts.note: tarts are pastries or cakes
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: extremely picks out the extreme letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Upside-down cakes with a single very fruity layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a noun in a cake; it is the verb to arrange in layers.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things in strata or tiers is to set them out in layers, so the verbs match.
